what_its_for: Methylergonovine is used to prevent and control serious bleeding from the uterus after childbirth or after a miscarriage or abortion. It works by causing the uterus to squeeze and contract, which helps stop heavy bleeding.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth exactly as your doctor prescribed. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food. Do not crush or chew the tablet. Take it at the same times each day to keep a steady level in your body.
dosing: The usual adult dose is one tablet (0.2 mg) taken 3 to 4 times a day. Your doctor will tell you exactly how many tablets to take and for how long, usually no longer than 1 week. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never take more than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store methylergonovine tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the tablets away from light, heat, and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of the reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid smoking while taking this medicine, as nicotine can make blood vessels narrow and increase your risk of serious side effects like reduced blood flow. Avoid drinking grapefruit juice, as it may increase the levels of this drug in your body. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as small amounts can pass into breast milk. Avoid taking other medicines that constrict blood vessels, such as certain migraine medications or decongestants, unless your doctor approves. Avoid alcohol as it may worsen dizziness.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: chest pain or tightness, sudden severe headache, shortness of breath, numbness or tingling in your hands or feet, fingers or toes turning blue or white, sudden vision changes, leg cramps or pain, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also call your doctor if your bleeding does not improve or gets worse, if you develop a fever, or if you feel unusually confused or dizzy.
when_it_works: Methylergonovine usually starts working within 5 to 10 minutes when taken by mouth. You should notice that your uterus feels firmer and that bleeding slows down. Most people take this medicine for a short time, usually up to 1 week after delivery. Talk to your doctor if you do not notice any improvement.
special_populations: Pregnancy: This medicine should NOT be used during pregnancy, as it can cause harmful uterine contractions and harm the baby. It is only used after the baby and placenta have been delivered. Breastfeeding: Small amounts of this drug may pass into breast milk and could cause side effects in a nursing baby. Talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits before breastfeeding. Older adults: Use with caution, as older adults may be more sensitive to the blood vessel effects of this medicine. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as dose adjustments may be needed. High blood pressure: This medicine can raise blood pressure, so it must be used very carefully in people who already have high blood pressure or preeclampsia.
